intro: You are standing before the Great Mosque and Hospital of Divriği, in Sivas province, built in 1228–1229. A mosque and a hospital, side by side, whose carved portals have no equal in Anatolia. It is no surprise that this was among the first sites in Türkiye inscribed by UNESCO.
history: In 1228–29 the Mengücekid ruler Ahmet Şah and his wife Turan Melek built a mosque and a hospital side by side: a place for prayer and a place for healing. What makes the complex singular is its portals. The North (Paradise), West (Textile) and Hospital doorways carry carved ornament of a depth and volume unmatched in Islamic architecture. And inside the hospital, it is said, patients were treated with music.
highlights: As you wander, don't miss the Paradise Portal and the Textile Portal, then the Hospital Portal. Step inside to see the wooden minbar, and end in the hospital courtyard.
facts: Did you know? On certain days of the year the sun casts, across the carving of the west portal, the silhouette of a figure at prayer — an effect taken to be part of the design. The carving on the portals is so deep that the stone reads as woven cloth; no other ornament in Islamic architecture works at this scale or with this freedom. And listen: the hospital is held to have treated patients with the sound of water and with music, its courtyard acoustics designed for that very purpose.
outro: This brings our journey through Divriği to an end. Before you go, a small request: please leave the stones untouched, keep to the marked paths and carry water with you. This carved stone has waited for centuries; let it keep waiting for those who come after you. Enjoy your visit.
